Explore data interactively

Source: R/eda_interactive.R
eda_explore.Rd

Opens a Shiny gadget (in the viewer pane by default) to explore the variables of a data set: select variables by name or label (or by a pattern, e.g. a whole item battery), choose a grouping variable (e.g. a cluster solution) and an optional weight, and get

  • plots of all selected variables in one plot (eda_plot()): horizontal or vertical bar charts of the means with or without error bars, boxplots, or stacked bar charts of the distributions;

  • descriptive statistics (eda_describe());

  • tests of group differences (eda_test(), see "Statistical tests" there), comparing each group with the total (default), the rest of the sample, the mean of the group means, or all other groups;

  • if ggstatsplot is installed, a detailed plot of a single variable with the test results (eda_plot_detail(); "Detailed plot" tab, customizable in the sidebar);

  • a codebook with the variable and value labels;

  • the code to reproduce the plot and the statistics in a script.

The plots can be downloaded as JPEG (ya_save_plot(), 300 dpi) and the statistics as Excel file. Click "Done" to close the gadget and return them to the console.

Usage

eda_explore(data = NULL, viewer = c("pane", "browser", "dialog"))

Arguments

data

Optional. A data frame or the output of seg_cluster() to show first. If NULL (default), the first data frame in the global environment is shown; all others can be selected in the gadget.

viewer

Where to show the gadget: "pane" (RStudio/Positron viewer pane, default), "browser" or "dialog".

Value

Invisibly, when closed with "Done": a list with plot (ggplot), describe (eda_describe() output) and code (character, the code to reproduce them). NULL if no variables were selected.

Details

The gadget lists all data frames and seg_cluster() outputs in the global environment. For a seg_cluster or seg_cluster_set, the original data of the clustered respondents is shown and each cluster solution is available as grouping variable (e.g. cluster_k4), see eda_describe().

Requires the packages shiny, bslib and DT; ggstatsplot is optional.

See also

Other eda: eda_describe(), eda_plot(), eda_plot_detail(), eda_test()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
eda_explore(sm_synthetic)

# With a cluster solution as grouping variable
prep <- seg_prep_data(sim_segments, vars = dplyr::starts_with("item_"), verbose = FALSE)
km <- seg_cluster(prep, k = 2:4, plots = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
eda_explore(km)
}
